A. Chapter Overview

Chapter Overview

Welcome to Chapter 3. In this chapter, you will learn how to write and understand procedure text. A procedure text gives clear instructions to help people do something step by step.

Selamat datang di Chapter 3. Pada bab ini, kalian akan belajar tentang procedure text, yaitu teks yang berisi petunjuk atau langkah-langkah untuk melakukan sesuatu.

Procedure text is very useful in daily life. You can use it to explain:

  • how to protect your personal data online;
  • how to communicate politely on social media;
  • how to create a safe password;
  • how to check information before sharing it;
  • how to make a healthy snack or drink;
  • how to record a tutorial video;
  • how to create a digital handbook.

Dalam kehidupan remaja saat ini, procedure text tidak hanya digunakan untuk resep makanan atau cara membuat sesuatu. Procedure text juga bisa digunakan untuk kecakapan hidup abad ke-21, seperti digital safety, digital etiquette, dan responsible online communication.

For students in island or coastal areas, digital communication can be very important. Sometimes, internet connection is limited. Students may use social media, chat groups, online classes, downloaded materials, or shared devices. Because of that, students need to know how to communicate clearly, safely, and respectfully online.

Big Question: How can we give clear instructions and communicate wisely in digital spaces?
Bagaimana kita dapat memberi instruksi yang jelas dan berkomunikasi dengan bijak di ruang digital?

Learning Objectives

After learning this chapter, you are expected to be able to:

  1. identify the social function of procedure text;

  2. analyze the structure of procedure text: goal, materials/tools, and steps;
    menganalisis struktur procedure text: tujuan, bahan/alat, dan langkah-langkah;

    memahami teks prosedur tentang keamanan digital, etika digital, dan kecakapan hidup praktis;
  4. use imperative sentences such as Do, Don’t, Check, Avoid, Use, Make sure, and Ensure;

    menggunakan penghubung urutan seperti First, Next, Then, After that, Finally;
  6. use adverbs of manner such as carefully, politely, clearly, safely, wisely, and responsibly;
    menggunakan adverb of manner seperti carefully, politely, clearly, safely, wisely, dan responsibly;
  7. give oral instructions clearly and respectfully;
    memberi instruksi lisan dengan jelas dan sopan;
  8. write a procedure text about digital etiquette or life skills;
    menulis procedure text tentang etika digital atau kecakapan hidup;
  9. create a tutorial video or digital handbook about wise social media use;
    membuat video tutorial atau buklet digital tentang penggunaan media sosial yang bijak;

C. Mindful Starter

Think Before You Click

Sebelum mempelajari procedure text, pikirkan beberapa situasi berikut. Situasi ini dekat dengan kehidupan remaja, terutama siswa yang menggunakan media sosial, grup kelas, dan internet untuk belajar.

Situation 1: A Class Group Message

A student receives a message in the class group. The message says that school will be closed tomorrow because of bad weather. However, there is no official announcement from school.

Think: Should the student share the message immediately? What should the student check first? How can the student respond politely?

Situation 2: A Shared Phone

Two students use the same phone to download learning materials because the internet signal is better in one place. One student accidentally sees the other student’s private chat.

Think: What should the student do? Why is privacy important? How can students share devices safely?

Situation 3: A Healthy Snack Tutorial

A group of students wants to make a short tutorial video about a healthy snack using local ingredients, such as banana, coconut, seaweed jelly, or boiled cassava.

Think: What instructions should they give? What sequence connectors can they use? How can they speak clearly in the video?

Reflection Questions

Jawablah secara singkat.

  1. What should you do before sharing information online?
    Apa yang harus kamu lakukan sebelum membagikan informasi daring?
  2. Why should you protect your password?
    Mengapa kamu harus melindungi kata sandi?
  3. How can you comment politely online?
    Bagaimana cara memberi komentar dengan sopan di internet?
  4. What procedure or tutorial have you watched before?
    Tutorial atau panduan apa yang pernah kamu tonton?
  5. What life skill do you want to explain in English?
    Kecakapan hidup apa yang ingin kamu jelaskan dalam Bahasa Inggris?

D–F. Concept

What Is Procedure Text?

Definition

Procedure text is a text that explains how to do, make, use, or operate something through clear steps.

Procedure text adalah teks yang menjelaskan cara melakukan, membuat, menggunakan, atau mengoperasikan sesuatu melalui langkah-langkah yang jelas.

Social Function

to tell readers or listeners how to do something correctly and safely.
memberi petunjuk kepada pembaca atau pendengar agar dapat melakukan sesuatu dengan benar dan aman.

Examples of Procedure Text

TopicExample Title
Digital safetyHow to Protect Your Personal Data Online
Digital etiquetteHow to Communicate Politely in a Class Group
Social media responsibilityHow to Post Wisely on Social Media
Information literacyHow to Check News Before Sharing It
Healthy foodHow to Make a Simple Banana-Coconut Snack
Study skillHow to Prepare for an Online Webinar
Tutorial videoHow to Record a Short Learning Vlog
Digital handbookHow to Create a Digital Safety Handbook

Why Is Procedure Text Important?

Procedure text is important because it helps people follow instructions, avoid mistakes, stay safe, understand steps clearly, complete a task, solve practical problems, and learn useful life skills.

Dalam kehidupan digital, procedure text membantu kita memahami cara menggunakan teknologi dengan aman, sopan, dan bertanggung jawab.

Structure of Procedure Text

1. Goal / Title

The goal tells what the text is about.

Example: How to Protect Your Personal Data Online

2. Materials / Tools / Requirements

This part lists what we need: phone, internet connection, strong password, trusted website, privacy setting, notebook, learning account, or cooking ingredients.

3. Steps / Methods

This part explains the actions in order. Steps often use imperative verbs, sequence connectors, and short clear sentences.

4. Tips / Warnings

Tips and warnings give extra advice to help readers avoid problems. This part is optional, but very useful for digital safety.

Procedure Text vs Recount Text

AspectRecount TextProcedure Text
PurposeTo retell past eventsTo explain how to do something
Main tenseSimple past tenseImperative sentences/simple present
Time focusPast experienceSteps or instructions
StructureOrientation, events, reorientationGoal, materials/tools, steps
Example titleMy First Webinar ExperienceHow to Join a Webinar Safely
Common verbsjoined, went, wrote, learnedopen, click, check, avoid, use

G–I. Grammar Lab

Grammar Lab: Imperatives, Sequence Connectors, and Adverbs

1. Imperative Sentences

An imperative sentence is a sentence that gives a command, instruction, request, or advice. Imperative sentence adalah kalimat yang memberi perintah, instruksi, permintaan, atau saran. In procedure text, imperative sentences are very common.

Positive Imperatives

Pattern: Verb 1 + Object/Complement

Imperative SentenceArti Bahasa Indonesia
Open your privacy settings.Buka pengaturan privasimu.
Check the source carefully.Periksa sumbernya dengan teliti.
Use a strong password.Gunakan kata sandi yang kuat.
Write your message politely.Tulis pesanmu dengan sopan.
Save your work regularly.Simpan pekerjaanmu secara berkala.
Read the instructions first.Baca instruksinya terlebih dahulu.
Prepare your materials.Siapkan bahan-bahanmu.
Wash your hands before cooking.Cuci tanganmu sebelum memasak.
Mix the ingredients slowly.Campur bahan-bahannya perlahan.
Speak clearly in your tutorial.Berbicaralah dengan jelas dalam tutorialmu.

Negative Imperatives

Pattern: Don’t + Verb 1 + Object/Complement

Negative ImperativeArti Bahasa Indonesia
Don’t share your password.Jangan membagikan kata sandimu.
Don’t post private information.Jangan mengunggah informasi pribadi.
Don’t insult people online.Jangan menghina orang di internet.
Don’t spread unverified news.Jangan menyebarkan berita yang belum terverifikasi.
Don’t click suspicious links.Jangan klik tautan mencurigakan.
Don’t use rude words.Jangan menggunakan kata-kata kasar.
Don’t record others without permission.Jangan merekam orang lain tanpa izin.
Don’t copy someone’s work without credit.Jangan menyalin karya orang lain tanpa mencantumkan sumber.
Don’t speak too fast in your video.Jangan berbicara terlalu cepat dalam videomu.
Don’t leave your account logged in on a shared device.Jangan biarkan akunmu tetap masuk di perangkat bersama.

Imperatives with “Do”

Do can make an instruction stronger, more encouraging, or more polite.

SentenceArti Bahasa Indonesia
Do check the source before sharing the news.Pastikan memeriksa sumber sebelum membagikan berita.
Do speak politely in the group chat.Pastikan berbicara dengan sopan di grup chat.
Do ask for permission before using someone’s photo.Pastikan meminta izin sebelum menggunakan foto orang lain.
Do save your file before closing the application.Pastikan menyimpan file sebelum menutup aplikasi.

Imperatives with “Ensure” and “Make Sure”

Ensure and make sure mean pastikan.

SentenceArti Bahasa Indonesia
Ensure your password is strong.Pastikan kata sandimu kuat.
Ensure your information is correct.Pastikan informasimu benar.
Ensure your video is respectful.Pastikan videomu sopan.
Make sure your caption is polite.Pastikan caption-mu sopan.
Make sure your account is logged out.Pastikan akunmu sudah keluar.
Make sure the recipe is safe and clean.Pastikan resepnya aman dan bersih.

Polite Imperatives

Polite InstructionArti Bahasa Indonesia
Please read the instructions carefully.Tolong baca instruksi dengan teliti.
Remember to check your privacy settings.Ingatlah untuk memeriksa pengaturan privasimu.
Try to write your message clearly.Cobalah menulis pesanmu dengan jelas.
Avoid sharing personal information.Hindari membagikan informasi pribadi.
Be careful to choose reliable sources.Berhati-hatilah memilih sumber tepercaya.

2. Sequence Connectors

Sequence connectors are words or phrases that show the order of steps. Procedure text needs sequence connectors because readers must follow the steps in the correct order.

Sequence ConnectorArti Bahasa IndonesiaFunctionExample
firstpertama-tamastarts the first stepFirst, open the settings menu.
secondkeduashows the second stepSecond, choose privacy.
nextberikutnyamoves to the next stepNext, change your password.
thenkemudianshows the next actionThen, save the changes.
after thatsetelah itucontinues the stepsAfter that, check your account.
beforesebelumshows earlier actionBefore posting, check your caption.
finallyakhirnyashows the last stepFinally, log out safely.
at the endpada akhircloses the procedureAt the end, review your work.
oncesetelahshows condition after something happensOnce the video is ready, upload it.
whenketikashows time/conditionWhen you receive a link, check it carefully.

Sequence Connectors in Procedure Text

SentenceArti Bahasa Indonesia
First, open your social media settings.Pertama, buka pengaturan media sosialmu.
Next, choose privacy and security.Berikutnya, pilih privasi dan keamanan.
Then, change your password.Kemudian, ubah kata sandimu.
After that, review your personal information.Setelah itu, tinjau informasi pribadimu.
Finally, save the changes.Akhirnya, simpan perubahan.

Less Clear

Open settings. Save changes. Change your password. Check privacy.

Better

First, open settings. Next, check privacy. Then, change your password. Finally, save the changes.

Versi kedua lebih jelas karena urutan langkahnya mudah diikuti.

3. Adverbs of Manner

Adverbs of manner describe how an action is done. Adverbs of manner menjelaskan bagaimana suatu tindakan dilakukan. Many adverbs of manner end in -ly.

Adverb of MannerArti Bahasa IndonesiaExample SentenceArti Kalimat

safelydengan amanLog out safely.Keluarlah dari akun dengan aman.
wiselydengan bijakUse social media wisely.Gunakan media sosial dengan bijak.
responsiblydengan bertanggung jawabShare information responsibly.Bagikan informasi dengan bertanggung jawab.

gentlydengan lembutStir the mixture gently.Aduk campurannya dengan lembut.
quicklydengan cepatSave the file quickly.Simpan file dengan cepat.
regularlysecara teraturUpdate your password regularly.Perbarui kata sandimu secara teratur.
privatelysecara pribadiSend private information privately, if necessary.Kirim informasi pribadi secara pribadi jika perlu.
respectfullydengan hormat/sopanComment respectfully.Berkomentarlah dengan sopan.
honestlydengan jujurWrite your report honestly.Tulis laporanmu dengan jujur.
calmlydengan tenangRespond calmly to criticism.Tanggapi kritik dengan tenang.
correctlydengan benarType your email correctly.Ketik emailmu dengan benar.

Position of Adverbs of Manner

PatternExampleArti
Verb + adverbSpeak clearly.Berbicaralah dengan jelas.
Verb + object + adverbCheck the source carefully.Periksa sumbernya dengan teliti.
Verb + object + adverbWrite your caption politely.Tulis caption-mu dengan sopan.
Verb + adverbReply calmly.Balaslah dengan tenang.

L–O. Model Texts

Model Procedure Texts

Model Text 1: How to Protect Your Personal Data Online

Goal

To protect your personal data when using social media, online learning platforms, or shared devices.

Tools / Requirements

  • a phone or laptop;
  • internet connection;
  • privacy settings;
  • strong password;
  • trusted information sources.

Steps

  1. First, use a strong password.
    Choose a password with letters, numbers, and symbols. Do not use your birthday, nickname, or school name as your password.
  2. Next, check your privacy settings carefully.
    Make sure only trusted people can see your private posts, photos, and personal information.
  3. Then, avoid sharing personal data publicly.
    Do not post your home address, phone number, student card, family problems, ticket number, or password online.
  4. After that, be careful with suspicious links.
    Check the sender and the website address before clicking a link. Do not click links that look strange or promise unrealistic prizes.
  5. Next, log out from shared devices.
    If you use a school computer, a friend’s phone, or a family device, make sure you log out safely after using your account.
  6. Finally, check your digital footprint regularly.
    Review your posts, comments, and profile. Delete or edit anything that may harm your privacy or reputation.

Tips / Warnings

  • Don’t share your password with anyone.
  • Don’t post private documents online.
  • Report suspicious accounts.
  • Ask a teacher or trusted adult if you are unsure.
  • Use social media wisely and responsibly.

Tools/Requirementsphone/laptop, internet, privacy settings, strong password

Model Text 2: How to Communicate Politely in a Class Group Chat

Goal

To help students communicate clearly, politely, and responsibly in a class group chat.

Tools / Requirements

  • a phone;
  • class group chat;
  • clear message;
  • polite words;
  • self-control.

Steps

  1. First, read the previous messages carefully.
    Make sure you understand the topic before replying.
  2. Next, write your message clearly.
    Use simple words. Avoid confusing sentences. If you ask about homework, mention the subject and the task.
  3. Then, use polite expressions.
    Use words such as “please,” “thank you,” “excuse me,” and “sorry.” These words make your message more respectful.
  4. After that, avoid rude words and personal attacks.
    Do not mock your friends, insult someone’s opinion, or embarrass others in the group.
  5. Next, check your message before sending it.
    Read it again. Make sure the tone is friendly and the information is correct.
  6. Finally, respond calmly if there is a misunderstanding.
    Explain your meaning politely. Do not continue an online argument.

Tips / Warnings

  • Don’t send messages late at night unless it is urgent.
  • Don’t spam the group with unrelated content.
  • Don’t share someone’s photo without permission.
  • Give feedback kindly.
  • Respect your teacher and classmates.

Model Text 3: How to Make a Simple Banana-Coconut Snack

Goal

To make a simple, healthy snack using local ingredients.

Ingredients / Tools

  • 2 ripe bananas;
  • 2 tablespoons of grated coconut;
  • 1 teaspoon of honey or palm sugar;
  • a small bowl;
  • a spoon;
  • a clean knife;
  • a plate.

Steps

  1. First, wash your hands carefully.
    Make sure your hands and tools are clean before preparing food.
  2. Next, peel the bananas.
    Put the bananas on a clean plate.
  3. Then, cut the bananas slowly.
    Use a clean knife and be careful.
  4. After that, add grated coconut.
    Spread the grated coconut evenly on top of the banana pieces.
  5. Next, add a little honey or palm sugar.
    Do not add too much sweetener. Keep the snack simple and healthy.
  6. Finally, serve the snack immediately.
    Enjoy it with a glass of water.

Tips / Warnings

  • Wash the knife and plate before using them.
  • Cut the banana carefully.
  • Don’t add too much sugar.
  • Use fresh ingredients.
  • Keep your cooking area clean.

Model Text 4: How to Check News Before Sharing It

Goal

To help students avoid spreading false information online.

Tools / Requirements

  • phone or laptop;
  • internet connection;
  • trusted news sources;
  • official school or government information channel;
  • careful reading habit.

Steps

  1. First, read the whole message carefully.
    Do not believe a message only because the title sounds urgent.
  2. Next, check who sent the message.
    Ask yourself: Is the sender reliable? Is the information from an official source?
  3. Then, compare the information with trusted sources.
    Check official school announcements, trusted news websites, or official government channels.
  4. After that, look at the date and details.
    Old information can become misleading if people share it again without context.
  5. Next, avoid adding dramatic words.
    Do not make the message sound more frightening or more exciting than it really is.
  6. Finally, share the information only if it is true and useful.
    If you are not sure, ask a teacher, parent, or trusted adult first.

Tips / Warnings

  • Don’t spread news only because it is viral.
  • Don’t share screenshots without checking the context.
  • Don’t create panic in class groups.
  • Check facts carefully.
  • Share information responsibly.

P. Reading Comprehension

Reading Comprehension

Text: How to Join an Online Webinar Safely

Goal

To help students join an online webinar safely and respectfully.

Tools / Requirements

You need a phone or laptop, internet connection, webinar link, notebook, pen, and earphones if available.

Steps

First, check the webinar information carefully. Make sure the link comes from your teacher, school, or a trusted organizer. Do not click a link from an unknown person.

Next, prepare your notebook and pen. Write the title of the webinar, the date, and the name of the speaker. If the internet connection is weak, sit in a place with a better signal.

Then, enter the webinar room politely. Use your real name if the teacher asks you to do so. Turn off your microphone when you are not speaking. Listen to the speaker carefully.

After that, write important points in your notebook. If you want to ask a question, use polite language. For example, you can write, “Excuse me, may I ask a question?”

Finally, leave the webinar room respectfully. Thank the speaker if possible. Review your notes and write one lesson that you learned from the webinar.

Tips

Don’t share the webinar link with strangers. Don’t record the webinar without permission. Don’t write rude comments in the chat box. Join the webinar responsibly and respectfully.

Reading Questions

  1. What is the goal of the procedure text?
  2. What tools do students need to join the webinar?
  3. Why should students check the webinar link carefully?
  4. What should students prepare before entering the webinar room?
  5. What should students do if the internet connection is weak?
  6. Why should students turn off the microphone when they are not speaking?
  7. What polite expression can students use to ask a question?
  8. What should students do after leaving the webinar room?
  9. Mention three things students should not do during the webinar.
  10. Find five imperative sentences from the text.
  11. Find five sequence connectors from the text.
  12. Find three adverbs of manner from the text.

Student Draft and Revised Version

Student Draft

How to safe in group chat. First, read message. Next, check source careful. Then, don’t rude comment. After that, reply polite. Finally, use group responsible. Don’t share password and don’t send hoax.

Revised Version

How to Stay Safe in a Class Group Chat

Goal: To help students use a class group chat safely and respectfully.

First, read the message carefully before replying. Next, check the source of the information. Make sure it comes from a teacher, school, or trusted person. Then, write your response politely. Don’t use rude words or personal attacks. After that, avoid sharing private information such as passwords, phone numbers, or home addresses. Finally, use the class group responsibly to ask questions, share learning information, and support your classmates.

Tips: Don’t spread hoaxes. Don’t share your password. Report harmful messages to your teacher. Always communicate politely and calmly.

ProblemExplanation
“How to safe”Gunakan verb: “How to stay safe.”
“read message”Perlu article/possessive: “read the message.”
“check source careful”Gunakan adverb: “check the source carefully.”
“don’t rude comment”Gunakan verb: “don’t write rude comments.”
“reply polite”Gunakan adverb: “reply politely.”
“use group responsible”Gunakan adverb: “use the group responsibly.”
Tips masih terlalu pendekTambahkan penjelasan agar lebih jelas.

Why Is the Revised Version Better?

  • it has a clear title;
  • it states the goal;
  • it uses sequence connectors;
  • it uses imperative sentences correctly;
  • it uses adverbs of manner: carefully, politely, responsibly, calmly;
  • it gives useful tips and warnings;
  • it sounds clearer and more respectful.

Digital Handbook: How to Use Social Media Wisely

Cover: Title: How to Use Social Media Wisely; Created by: __________; Class: X __________

Introduction: Social media can help students learn, communicate, and share positive ideas. However, students must use it carefully and responsibly.

Procedure:
First, think before posting.
Next, check your privacy settings.
Then, write comments politely.
After that, check information before sharing it.
Finally, use social media to learn and create positive content.

Tips:

  • Don’t share your password.
  • Don’t post private information.
  • Don’t spread hoaxes.
  • Ask for permission before posting someone’s photo.
  • Give credit when using other people’s work.

What Is a Tutorial Video?

A tutorial video is a video that shows how to do something step by step. Your tutorial video can be simple. You do not need expensive tools. You can use a phone, natural light, a quiet place, short script, simple visuals, and clear voice.

Common Mistakes in Procedure Text

1. Using Past Tense Instead of Imperative

IncorrectCorrectExplanation
You opened the settings.Open the settings.Procedure text uses imperatives.
You checked the source.Check the source.Use Verb 1.
You saved the file.Save the file.Give direct instruction.

2. Missing Sequence Connectors

Less ClearBetter
Open the app. Check privacy. Save changes.First, open the app. Next, check privacy. Finally, save changes.

3. Wrong Adverb Form

IncorrectCorrectExplanation
Reply polite.Reply politely.Use adverb of manner.
Check careful.Check carefully.Use -ly form.
Speak clear.Speak clearly.Use adverb, not adjective.
Use social media wise.Use social media wisely.Use “wisely.”

4. Too General Instructions

Too GeneralBetter
Be good online.Write polite comments and avoid rude words.
Stay safe.Don’t share your password or home address online.
Check information.Compare the message with official school announcements.

5. Unsafe Digital Advice

UnsafeBetter
Share your password with close friends.Don’t share your password with anyone.
Click every link quickly.Check suspicious links carefully before clicking.
Post your friend’s photo without asking.Ask for permission before posting someone’s photo.

Final product: Digital Etiquette Tutorial or Handbook. Students submit one of the following: tutorial video script and video plan, digital handbook draft, or printed handbook page if digital tools are limited.

AG–AH. Teacher’s Key & Sources

Teacher’s Key & Source References

Teacher’s Key – Hide This Section If Used for Students

Reading Comprehension Key

  1. To help students join an online webinar safely and respectfully.
  2. Phone or laptop, internet connection, webinar link, notebook, pen, and earphones if available.
  3. To make sure the link comes from a teacher, school, or trusted organizer.
  4. Notebook and pen.
  5. Sit in a place with a better signal.
  6. To avoid disturbing the speaker and other participants.
  7. “Excuse me, may I ask a question?”
  8. Review notes and write one lesson learned.
  9. Don’t share the webinar link with strangers; don’t record without permission; don’t write rude comments.
  10. Examples: Check the webinar information carefully; Make sure the link comes from your teacher; Prepare your notebook and pen; Use your real name; Turn off your microphone; Listen carefully; Write important points; Thank the speaker.
  11. First, Next, Then, After that, Finally.
  12. carefully, politely, respectfully, responsibly.

Listening Gap Filling Key

  1. group
  2. politely
  3. family
  4. carefully
  5. trusted
  6. calmly
  7. adult
  8. responsibly

Listening Sequencing Key

C - B - E - D - A

Vocabulary Builder Key

Activity 1: 1. B; 2. A; 3. C; 4. D; 5. E

Activity 2: 1. carefully; 2. politely; 3. safely; 4. responsibly; 5. clearly

Activity 3: 1. B; 2. B; 3. C

Activity 4 Possible Answers: Check the link carefully. Reply to the message politely. Use social media wisely. Speak clearly in your tutorial. Save your file regularly.

Remedial Key

Imperative Practice: 1. Check the source. 2. Write your message politely. 3. Save your file. 4. Don’t share your password. 5. Ask for permission.

Adverb Practice: 1. B; 2. B; 3. B; 4. A; 5. A

Digital spaces are part of our daily life. Use them wisely. Communicate politely. Protect your privacy. A good instruction can help people stay safe, learn better, and respect each other.
Be clear. Be kind. Be responsible online.
